rv.q: Instead, Nicholls, along with directors Aneesha Srinivasan and David Byrne, have created a strange, macabre, properly funny piece of theatre about the human condition that ponders on the future as much as the past.
This feral story soars with untamed life.
It’s a promising debut and just the sort of premiere the Royal Court should be staging in its tiny upstairs studio as it turns 70.
The Shitheads is the epitome of a big swing that paid off: this weird, not-so-little debut play deserves to be a benchmark for those making new work that thinks outside the box.
The clear, confident performance with some fine puppetry held the audience’s attention.

The production, co-directed by Aneesha Srinivasan and Royal Court artistic director David Byrne, struggles to keep up the early momentum and by the – predictably violent – climax, my emotional investment had waned.
But the overall image of violent brutality reflects less the origins of our species and more our current nihilism and despair.
Nicholls writes with such assurance that he crafts a convincing and compelling primitive world that is also very modern.
Fizzing with ideas and admirably ambitious, this is an exciting and undoubtedly promising debut from Nicholls.

cn.t: Jack Nicholls' audacious prehistoric debut divides critics with its darkly comic, unpredictable vision of early humans. Praised for its originality and macabre humor, though some find its nihilistic approach less successful.
